title: Shallow unlearning
description: Targeted knowledge can remain recoverable after unlearning interventions.
bottom_line: Unlearning can bring accuracy on targeted knowledge near chance while largely preserving general ability, but independent groups have recovered performance through fine-tuning on few examples and edits to models' internal activity. Recovery depends on the method, model and relearning data; recovery from small sets above 10 billion parameters remains uncertain. Claims of resistance to recovery attacks remain contested, and recovery alone does not establish that knowledge was retained. Clearer recovery budgets, matched attack comparisons, separation of evaluations and confirmation that apparent replications use independent experiments are still needed.

claims.heading: Unlearning can bring target accuracy near chance, preserve general ability, and resist simple attacks
claims.summary: Independent groups reproduce near-chance accuracy on the knowledge targeted for removal, with general ability largely preserved. Resistance to simple attacks is contested when these include fine-tuning on a few examples or edits made with access to the model's internals.

claims.heading: Small fine-tuning sets can restore knowledge after unlearning
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce recovery from small relearning sets in models up to 10B parameters, including recovery of held-out facts. Success depends on the unlearning method and relearning data; unrelated data do not consistently work, and small-set recovery above 10B remains uncertain.

claims.heading: Internal edits can recover knowledge after unlearning
claims.summary: Several independent groups recovered performance after RMU unlearning by removing a direction from the model's internal activations (activation-direction ablation), with results on Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Recovery depends on the method and model; broader evidence that unlearning blocks access to retained knowledge is mostly correlational.

claims.heading: Low-bit quantization, which reduces weight precision, can restore forgotten information
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce recovery on the MUSE and TOFU benchmarks after 4-bit quantization, which reduces the precision of model weights. Recovery depends on the unlearning method and quantization setup, with conflicting MUSE results and mostly weak or absent recovery on the WMDP knowledge benchmark.

claims.heading: Prompts can partially recover knowledge after unlearning
claims.summary: Several independent groups reproduce prompt-only recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, translation or added context. Recovery is usually partial and depends on the unlearning method and attack; some methods resist it.

claims.heading: Newer unlearning methods claim resistance to recovery attacks
claims.summary: Claims of attack-resistant unlearning are contested: independent groups have broken several defenses using attacks they were designed to resist. Some methods withstand narrower tests, while most newer methods have been tested only by their authors.

related_findings.title: Forgetting can come at a cost to utility
related_findings.summary: Without attacks, strong measured forgetting often accompanies lost general ability. Runs that preserve general ability can still perform better than random guessing, and RMU reruns depend on implementation and training settings.

examples.headline: GA, WGA and GD reach near-chance WMDP accuracy while sharply reducing MMLU.
Retain regularization preserves more MMLU performance but leaves higher WMDP-Bio accuracy in RMU reruns.
LoRA runs preserving general ability still perform better than random guessing on WMDP.

related_findings.title: Signs of training-data membership persist and can mislead
related_findings.summary: Tests for training-data membership can still distinguish data the model was trained to forget after answer accuracy or memorization falls. These tests can perform worse than random guessing or flag examples never used in training, complicating their interpretation.

examples.headline: For several methods, training-data membership tests retain near-original AUC despite lower answer accuracy.
GA GDR and NPO GDR reduce verbatim memorization while leaving substantial privacy leakage.
Membership tests repeatedly flag some images targeted for forgetting even in models never trained on them.

related_findings.title: Nearby retained knowledge can suffer
related_findings.summary: Unlearning can impair answers to harmless questions about topics close to the target. General ability benchmarks sometimes show much smaller changes than tests of this related knowledge.

examples.headline: Unlearning harms answers to related harmless questions more than general benchmark results suggest.
Unlearning in vision-language models harms related harmless responses; one setting preserves general ability but barely forgets.
Zephyr RMU sharply reduces accuracy on harmless questions bordering the target despite a small MMLU decline.

related_findings.title: Internal changes can leave target representations largely intact
related_findings.summary: Internal analyses often locate changes in late layers or an injected direction. Hidden states and answer rankings can remain close to the original model.

examples.headline: Ablating RMU's injected direction restores most activation similarity and baseline-like norms.
Hidden-state tests using perturbed prompts suggest URL memorization persists after RMU and NPO-KL.
Unlearned facts retain similar hidden states, while popular answers barely shift rank.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Low answer scores can hide signs of target retention
related_findings.summary: Even without an attack, low answer accuracy or little word-for-word reproduction can coexist with target information in reasoning, reworded outputs or rankings of possible answers. Some tests of these signals need comparison conditions to establish that knowledge was retained.

examples.headline: AnswerIDK sharply reduces final-answer accuracy while leaving substantial target information in reasoning.
DPO reduces verbatim book continuation while paraphrase reproduction remains near baseline.
Head-conditioned answer ranking stays high after NPO; authors caution this does not establish retained knowledge.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Suppressed harmful behavior can return
related_findings.summary: Benign or harmful fine-tuning and weight edits can restore harmful compliance after safety training. Resistance differs across methods and training implementations.

examples.headline: Benign Alpaca fine-tuning substantially reduces refusal in Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
RepNoise loses much of its protection under harmful fine-tuning or benign examples.
Weight orthogonalization restores harmful compliance after NPO safety training but leaves RepBend largely resistant.

related_findings.title: Internal diagnostics offer limited predictions of recovery
related_findings.summary: Information that remains and patterns of activation changes can track vulnerability to recovery. Predicting which individual facts will return remains difficult.

examples.headline: Remaining information about training-data membership correlates more strongly with attack success than membership-inference scores.
Relearning preferentially restores leading activation components where unlearning changes concentrate.
Access to model internals before attacks barely predicts which individual facts return.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Evaluation artifacts can mimic forgetting and recovery
related_findings.summary: An attack can succeed because it supplies answer clues or uses a test better able to elicit answers. Either can make apparent recovery harder to interpret as evidence that target knowledge was retained.

examples.headline: A prefix optimized using a model overfit to test data raises the base model's WMDP-Bio accuracy.
Soft tokens elicit arbitrary ASCII strings, weakening retention claims based solely on attack success.
Stronger tests using paraphrases and in-context examples also raise accuracy in models never subjected to unlearning.

related_findings.title: Measured forgetting depends on training choices
related_findings.summary: Sampling, reference models and intervention strength can substantially change measured forgetting. Similar utility scores do not guarantee similar forgetting outcomes.

examples.headline: Changing sampling of data to forget or retain substantially improves forgetting over standard paired sampling.
Perturbing NPO's reference model sharply reduces forgetting quality while general ability changes little.
Clamping a feature to a large negative value changes one answer; zeroing it leaves it unchanged.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Unchanged weights can still produce strong forgetting scores
related_findings.summary: Filters, routing and steering can achieve strong benchmark scores without removing knowledge from model weights. Prompt changes can partly bypass a learned gate.

examples.headline: An exact-name filter achieves near-perfect TOFU abstention and retained-data accuracy without unlearning data.
An inference-time filter reaches near-chance WMDP scores by answering flagged questions randomly.
Jailbreak templates reduce how often an input-conditioned steering gate activates on forget queries.

related_findings.title: Approximate unlearning leaves traces unlike retraining
related_findings.summary: Approximate unlearning can leave weights and output distributions distinguishable from those of a model retrained without the target data. Matching loss on data targeted for forgetting alone does not establish equivalent behavior.

examples.headline: Core-token confidence tests separate approximate unlearners, but not retraining, from a corrected original model.
Matching retrained-model loss on data targeted for forgetting still leaves substantial differences in output distributions.
Image unlearners remain far from retrained weights and usually closer to original weights.

related_findings.title: Target properties and training history shape forgetting
related_findings.summary: Unlearning outcomes depend on how targets were learned and how common they are. Training order can also determine whether alternative expressions of a target remain likely.

examples.headline: Locally grokked TOFU examples reach lower post-unlearning ES than ungrokked examples.
Training order determines whether an alternative compliance phrasing remains likely after GA.
Popular facts retain higher paraphrase recall than rare facts after NPO.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Recovery resistance needs utility and learning controls
related_findings.summary: Data filtering can reduce later acquisition of excluded capabilities, but related-data fine-tuning can still recover them. Low relearning can also reflect a reduced ability to learn new tasks.

examples.headline: Filtered Evo2-7B regains excluded viral capability through fine-tuning on related biological groups.
Larger data-filtered models learn less excluded-domain knowledge and resist elicitation through fine-tuning more than smaller models.
Low relearning without replaying past training examples accompanies reduced ability to learn new tasks.

related_findings.title: Poor output quality can produce apparent forgetting
related_findings.summary: Low scores on data targeted for forgetting can result from repetitive, illegible or irrelevant output. Such behavior differs from answering like a model that never learned the target.

examples.headline: Gradient difference combines high forgetting efficacy with extreme perplexity and reduced token diversity.
R2MU's non-leaking forget responses consist almost entirely of collapsed reasoning.
RMU safety unlearning produces mainly irrelevant responses to harmful queries rather than refusals.

related_findings.title: Forgetting transfers unevenly across modalities and languages
related_findings.summary: Forgetting through one type of input can leave the same facts accessible through another. Forgetting conditioned on language can instead spread beyond the requested language and affect related knowledge.

examples.headline: A universal image perturbation partially restores forgotten answers and factuality in multimodal models.
Strong forgetting on image-and-text queries leaves the same facts accessible through text alone.
Forgetting conditioned on language spreads to other languages and matched related knowledge.

related_findings.title: Recovery extends beyond language models
related_findings.summary: Image and federated models can retain or rapidly reacquire target behavior after approximate unlearning. Other audits find no recovery under the tested intervention.

examples.headline: FedAvg averages remaining clients' models, leaving substantial backdoor success; additional interventions eliminate it.
Reintroducing full target-class data rapidly restores ResNet-50 accuracy after class unlearning.
Rebuilding batch-normalization state changes general ability without restoring target-class accuracy in tested checkpoints.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Precision changes can expose suppressed knowledge
related_findings.summary: Small unlearning updates can disappear when quantization rounds weights into bins. Precision changes can also restore target outputs or increase signals that the model recognizes target information.

examples.headline: GA-GDR weight changes are too small for quantization to distinguish, leaving nearly identical quantized weight bins.
Switching to bfloat16 restores a target address after GA and NPO, while ReLearn remains stable.
NF4 raises J-space SafetyAUC for Qwen3-1.7B-abliterated, a recognition analogue of recovery.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Related knowledge can survive target removal
related_findings.summary: Unlearning a target need not remove supporting or implied facts. Models can still apply a supposedly forgotten algorithm, although some studies measure supporting knowledge without testing target recovery.

examples.headline: Models still solve some algorithm-dependent applications despite high judged forgetting rates.
Target-only unlearning incompletely weakens supporting facts; LoRA can strengthen remaining paths, without measured target recovery.
Forgetting a relationship leaves its implied relationship unchanged in the nested dataset.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Recovery alone does not establish retained knowledge
related_findings.summary: Models never trained on the target can still answer target questions or improve through related examples. Rapid relearning also depends on parameterization, so speed alone is insufficient evidence of retention.

examples.headline: Phi-1.5, never trained on TOFU, improves on held-out questions after fine-tuning on related benchmark items.
A retain-only model answers some direct and indirect TOFU questions targeted for forgetting.
Specially constructed model releases can recover rapidly even when their representations contain zero information about labels.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Later updates can revive earlier targets
related_findings.summary: Further unlearning requests and regularization on data meant to be retained can bring back previously suppressed outputs. This makes forgetting dependent on the model's subsequent training history.

examples.headline: Unlearning later tasks raises accuracy on a previously forgotten task.
Sequential diffusion concept erasure weakens forgetting of earlier targets.
Adding losses on data meant to be retained raises target ROUGE-L during unlearning.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Agent memory and retrieval can preserve forgotten information
related_findings.summary: External memory and retrieval can expose target information even when model answers suppress it. Information returned by tools and stored context therefore need separate evaluation from final answers.

examples.headline: Memory context raises F1 on data to forget in most tested checkpoints; tool access lowers it.
StaR reduces information leaked in answers; tool outputs still leak heavily, leaving overall leakage unchanged.
An instruction to forget an in-context record still leaves its target extractable.

related_findings.title: Sampling can reveal answers hidden by greedy decoding
related_findings.summary: Repeatedly sampling outputs can expose target answers missed when evaluation always chooses the most probable next token. Methods that explicitly control this generation process can reduce the gap.

examples.headline: Repeated sampling substantially increases success on data targeted for forgetting before any attack.
Sampling can trigger sensitive continuations, with top-p affecting leakage more than temperature.
Entropy minimization and adaptive temperature thresholding reduce sampled leakage to greedy levels.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Erased image concepts can reappear
related_findings.summary: Adversarial prompts, adjacent concepts and later fine-tuning can expose erased diffusion concepts. Recovery varies substantially across erasure methods.

examples.headline: Adversarial prompts recover nudity much more often from ESD than ACE.
After suppressing nudity generation, related-concept prompts still produce images flagged for nudity, at method-dependent rates.
Later fine-tuning revives erased objects for some diffusion methods, while others show no resurgence.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Deliberately hidden capabilities remain recoverable
related_findings.summary: Password locks can hide capabilities behind a password, while circuit breakers can suppress their use; fine-tuning or edits to internal activations can reveal these capabilities. Recovery varies by task, and correct answers can remain highly recognizable in the model's internal representations.

examples.headline: Edits to selected internal pathways recover password-locked capabilities; noise and random directions do little.
Small demonstration sets unlock password-locked capabilities; tasks differ in examples needed and how recovery carries over.
After circuit breakers suppress capabilities, correct answers remain highly recognizable in gemma-2-9b's internal representations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Internal edits can restore performance on material targeted for unlearning
related_findings.summary: Changes to activations, embeddings or model weights can partly restore performance on material targeted for unlearning. The effects depend on the intervention and its settings.

examples.headline: Activation changes raise target-text overlap (ROUGE-L) in some unlearned models, depending on layer and noise.
Attacks altering internal layers and embeddings raise WMDP-Bio biology accuracy, sometimes outperforming attacks altering model inputs.
Projecting GradDiff weights onto directions mapped to zero sharply restores accuracy on data targeted for unlearning.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fine-tuning provides a strong recovery test
related_findings.summary: Fine-tuning often matches or exceeds input-space attacks and can recover both unlearned and safety-trained models. Internal readouts can still distinguish those methods, while metric stability measures something different from recovery.

examples.headline: Few-example fine-tuning similarly restores capabilities after DPO, RMU and NPO, despite differing internal predictions (Logit Lens).
The stronger fine-tuning attack matches or beats attacks altering model inputs on nearly all tested models.
Metric correlations before and after unlearning test whether scores track together, rather than whether knowledge returns.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Prompt choice changes measured knowledge remaining after unlearning
related_findings.summary: Rephrased and adversarial prompts can reveal more information targeted for unlearning than direct queries, and gender prediction after unlearning also varies with the prompt. Fine-tuning against the prompts that yield the most accurate gender predictions reduces the highest prediction accuracy.

examples.headline: For GA (gradient ascent), the balance between forgetting and usefulness worsens under jailbreak and rephrased prompts.
Gender prediction varies across prompts after unlearning; fine-tuning against the highest-accuracy prompt lowers maximum accuracy.
Adversarial questions yield higher target-text overlap (ROUGE) than plain questions after ReRULE and RULE unlearning.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Models saved before and after unlearning can reveal forgotten text
related_findings.summary: Access to models saved before and after unlearning can enable reconstruction of forgotten text. Retraining from scratch without the forgotten data reduces extraction compared with editing an existing model to approximate that retraining, but does not always eliminate it.

examples.headline: Combining pre/post-unlearning models improves text extraction, even when unlearning exactly matches retraining without the targeted data.
TRACE reconstructs forgotten text from models before/after unlearning; retraining from scratch without it greatly lowers extraction.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Edited facts can resurface through alternative inputs
related_findings.summary: Knowledge edits can leave original answers accessible through changed prompts or different ways of splitting text into tokens. In one comparison, fine-tuning reduces bypass through these token splits more than MEMIT, a knowledge-editing method, but causes greater side effects elsewhere.

examples.headline: Prompts expressing doubt recover original answers after knowledge editing; one prompt includes the original answer.
Targeted fine-tuning reduces bypass through different token splits more than MEMIT editing, with larger side effects.

reading_list.why: Introduces the WMDP knowledge benchmark and RMU unlearning method, establishing original forgetting results examined by later stress tests.
Tests the released RMU unlearning model using few-example fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation (removing activation directions), and optimized prompts, finding substantial recovery.
Reports weaker recovery using GCG to find prompts eliciting forgotten knowledge from the previously evaluated released RMU model; evaluations disagree.

known_gaps.summary: The evidence still needs clearer recovery budgets and evaluation separation, matched attack comparisons, and confirmation that apparent replications use independent experiments.
items: Reinforcement-learning recovery after LUNAR unlearning uses prompts about the knowledge targeted for removal and a reward based on answers. The number of training examples and the separation between training and evaluation are unstated.

Assessments of the LUNAR unlearning method's robustness still need to incorporate outside reinforcement-learning results and ablation tests, which remove parts of the model's internal computation. Its own reverse attack to recover knowledge has already been compared with ablation tests using privileged information (oracle-guided) or no such information (blind), but matched comparisons across attacks remain incomplete.
Some apparent disagreements compare different models, benchmarks and unlearning settings. It remains unclear which reflect conflicting findings and which reflect sensitivity to those choices.
Some reports appear to reuse the same recovery experiments. It remains unclear whether those experiments were conducted independently, limiting how strongly the reports establish replication.
